subject: MAP: AWS Private Offer — Evaluation milestones & staged commit proposal
messages:
From: Sarah Young <sarah.young@acme-robotics.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.example
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme-robotics.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood MAP & private offer — eval timeline

Marcus — thanks again for the demo last week. As discussed, Acme is ready to run a 4-week evaluation but procurement will only sign if we can align a MAP with clear milestones that map to a staged private offer in AWS Marketplace.

High level asks from our side:
- 4-week eval plan (performance targets + sample prompts)
- Staged commit schedule tied to milestones (pilot -> ramp -> steady state)
- Indicative private offer pricing tiers and what discounts unlock at each commit
- A sample PO template and expected SSO/metering details for AWS private offers

I attached a one-page MAP template we use. Can Redwood propose a staged pricing ladder we can take to procurement? Our legal timeline is tight — hope to close commercial terms by EOM.

Thanks,
Sarah Young
Head of AI Platforms | Acme Robotics

Attachment: MAP_Acme_v1.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example>
To: Sarah Young <sarah.young@acme-robotics.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme-robotics.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.example
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood MAP & private offer — eval timeline

Sarah — appreciate the clear asks. Drafting a MAP + staged pricing we can align with an AWS private offer. Initial proposal below (summary; I'll attach a formal MAP and a redlined private-offer term sheet by Friday):

Proposed 4-week evaluation (week-by-week):
- Week 0 (prep): account onboarding, sampling prompts, baseline latency/cost measurement
- Week 1 (smoke tests): correctness checks, basic perf targets (p50 token latency < 120ms at 1rps)
- Week 2 (load): scaled throughput testing, autoscaling validations
- Week 3 (quality + edge cases): regen tests, hallucination spot checks; build evaluation report
- Week 4 (hand-off): final report, decision checklist for procurement

Staged commit proposal (AWS private offer tie-ins):
- Pilot (month 1-3): $25k commit (5% off list) — unlocks pilot SKU and priority onboarding
- Ramp (months 4-6): additional $75k commit (10% cumulative off list) — infrastructure credit for burst months
- Steady state (annual): commit $300k+ (20% cumulative off list) — reserved capacity pricing + access to dedicated support windows

Operational notes for Marketplace private offer:
- We can issue a private offer with tiered SKUs. Private Offer will reflect committed monthly minimums and auto-apply discounts when cumulative commit thresholds met.
- Billing flow: AWS invoice (customer) -> Redwood invoice reconciliation. PO should reference the private-offer id (we'll provide on signature).

Next steps: Neha (cc) will produce the MAP workbook with measurable success criteria and a draft private-offer term sheet. Can you confirm procurement contact and the ideal close date? You mentioned EOM — is that Feb 28?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: rdw-private-offer-draft-terms.pdf (pdf)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.example
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: MAP workbook + pricing ladder (draft)

Team — quick internal sync so external comms stay tight. I drafted a MAP workbook that maps each eval milestone to an acceptance criterion and the exact billing trigger for the private offer discounts. Key points we should be explicit about in the external MAP:

- Acceptance criteria must be measurable (example: 95% of prompts within acceptable intent/QA score >= 0.85; throughput >= X tokens/sec under Y concurrency)
- Discount unlocks should be backward-looking by billing period (i.e., if Pilot metrics met, discount applies to next invoice cycle)
- We should offer a one-time infrastructure credit (up to $8k) during Ramp to offset initial burst costs — helps procurement sign faster
- Include escrow-like language for sample data retention and SOC-2 evidence references to reduce legal friction

I've attached the workbook and a short FAQ for Procurement (how private offers work on AWS, required PO fields). Marcus — propose we send the formal MAP to Sarah on Friday morning with the private-offer scaffolding and a suggested legal owner for review.

-Neha
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachment: MAP_workbook_marcus_v1.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Sarah Young <sarah.young@acme-robotics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme-robotics.com>, procurement@acme-robotics.com
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood MAP & private offer — eval timeline

Marcus/Neha — this looks exactly like what procurement wanted. Two quick clarifications before we route to legal and procurement:
1) For the Pilot $25k commit, procurement wants that to be refundable if perf targets are not met after Week 4. Would Redwood be comfortable with a refund-if-fail clause tied to the MAP acceptance checklist?
2) For the Ramp infrastructure credit — can the credit be applied as an AWS credit line, or does it need to be an offset on Redwood's invoices?

If both are OK, procurement will start the PO thread. Our target is to have a signed private offer and PO by Feb 28 so we can start the pilot in March.

Thanks,
Sarah
Head of AI Platforms | Acme Robotics

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example>
To: Sarah Young <sarah.young@acme-robotics.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme-robotics.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.example, lauren_bishop@redwood.example
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: FINAL: MAP + private-offer scaffolding + next steps (PO template)

Sarah — attaching the finalized MAP workbook and a private-offer scaffold that maps the three tiers to AWS SKU IDs and indicative pricing. Answers to your questions:

1) Refund-if-fail for Pilot: Redwood can accept a partial refund model — if Week 4 acceptance criteria fail on clearly measurable items in the MAP workbook, we will refund up to 80% of the Pilot commit within 30 days. The remaining 20% covers infra/operational onboarding fees. We clarified the exact failure modes in section 3 of the workbook.

2) Ramp credit mechanics: credit will be applied as an offset on Redwood invoices (we cannot directly issue AWS account credits). We explicitly document the offset process in the private-offer term sheet so procurement can reconcile in one place.

Attached: MAP_Acme_final.xlsx, rdw-private-offer-Acme-SCA.pdf, PO_template_Acme.docx

Next steps:
- Procurement (Acme) to issue PO referencing Private Offer ID (we will supply the ID upon signature)
- Legal exchange: Redwood legal to send final private-offer signature package (DocuSign link) after PO is received
- Kickoff call: proposed Mon, Mar 1 — we will send calendar invite once PO is in place

If procurement wants minor changes to the refund clause, we can accept them as long as acceptance criteria remain measurable and timeboxed.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the pilot started.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_Acme_final.xlsx (xlsx); rdw-private-offer-Acme-SCA.pdf (pdf); PO_template_Acme.docx (docx)
